Eliot  appreciated the call earlier. Follow-ups and operational clarifications:

- Credit math (example): For a $120k monthly invoice, a single month of availability at 99.9% vs 99.95% would imply an annualized delta in expected outage minutes of ~262 -> ~131 minutes; our standard credit table would produce a prorated bill credit (example rows in the PDF). We included a per-1M-token marginal cost: 99.9 -> +$0.008 / 1k tokens; 99.95 -> +$0.018 / 1k tokens (illustrative).
- Escalation coverage: three bands  Business-hours (0917 PT, 24/5), Extended (1602 PT overlap for APAC), and 24x7 with on-call rotation. The retainer buys guaranteed SLA response times: 2 hours for Sev 1 on Business-hours, 1 hour for 24x7. On-call hours are tracked in our ticketing system and are invoiced monthly against the retainer.
- Roll-forward specifics: If you sign the 12-month Dedicated commit + 24x7 retainer, we can allow up to 25% of unused retainer hours to roll to the next quarter; any roll-forward beyond that would be a case-by-case credit applied to next invoice.

Two asks from our side:
1) Let us know which availability band you want priced into the contract (99.9 or 99.95).
2) If procurement needs a cap on total credits per year (finance-friendly), tell us a percentage threshold and we'll bake it into the SOW.

 Ben
